section_summary: This final section shifts from arrangements surrounding a British message for the dedication of a shrine to Admiral Tōgō to extensive documentation of the death of Prince Iesato Tokugawa. It records American condolences, Japanese acknowledgments, correspondence with the Tokugawa family, an America-Japan Society resolution, and newspaper accounts of Tokugawa’s life and funeral. Cross-reference and charge sheets conclude the file.

subfiles.title: Telegram concerning a British message for the Admiral Tōgō shrine dedication
subfiles.about: Reports British decisions concerning a message and representation at the dedication of a shrine to Admiral Tōgō.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports that the British ambassador submitted to the Japanese Foreign Ministry a proposed message from the First Lord of the Admiralty for the shrine dedication. The British naval attaché was authorized to attend, but the contemplated grant was abandoned.

subfiles.title: Subject jacket: Death of Prince Tokugawa
subfiles.about: Identifies the file subject as the death of the Japanese Prince Tokugawa.
subfiles.summary: The jacket establishes the new alphabetical subject concerning Prince Tokugawa’s death. It bears the date June 5, 1940, and instructions protecting the enclosed papers.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 182 ordering condolences for Prince Tokugawa
subfiles.about: Directs the embassy to express official American sympathy following Prince Tokugawa’s death.
subfiles.summary: Hull asks the embassy, unless it perceives an objection, to convey condolences to Tokugawa’s family and the Japanese government. He praises Tokugawa as a humanitarian, statesman, and advocate of friendly international relations and requests a report of the action taken.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 420 reporting delivery of condolences
subfiles.about: Confirms that Hull’s condolence message was sent to the Japanese foreign minister and Tokugawa family.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports that he sent separate letters to the Minister for Foreign Affairs and the family of Prince Tokugawa. Both letters conveyed Hull’s official message of sympathy.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to planned radio tribute by Viscount Inoue
subfiles.about: Refers to a telegram about arrangements for a July 5 radio tribute to Prince Tokugawa.
subfiles.summary: The sheet points to telegram No. 456 in file 894.76/13 concerning a tribute by Viscount Inoue for broadcast to the United States. Ambassador Grew had been asked to participate and requested instructions.

subfiles.title: Press release No. 272 on American condolences
subfiles.about: Announces that Ambassador Grew conveyed official American sympathy for Prince Tokugawa’s death.
subfiles.summary: The release states that Grew acted under the Secretary of State’s instructions in approaching the foreign minister and Tokugawa family. It describes Tokugawa as a great humanitarian, statesman, and advocate of international cooperation.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4772: Death of Prince Iesato Tokugawa
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits the embassy’s record of condolences and related materials concerning Prince Tokugawa’s death.
subfiles.summary: Grew refers to the Department’s instruction and his telegram confirming that the condolence message had been conveyed. He forwards seven items of correspondence and a group of Japan Advertiser clippings documenting reactions to Tokugawa’s death and funeral.

subfiles.title: Statement to the press on Prince Tokugawa’s death
subfiles.about: Offers Grew’s personal and official tribute to Prince Iesato Tokugawa.
subfiles.summary: Grew says that he and his wife were profoundly shocked by the death of a man whom he had known for eight years. He praises Tokugawa’s work as president of the America-Japan Society and extends sympathy to both the family and Japan.

subfiles.title: Personal letter of condolence to Prince Iemasa Tokugawa
subfiles.about: Conveys the Grews’ personal sympathy to Iemasa Tokugawa and his family.
subfiles.summary: Grew recalls his friendship and cooperation with Iemasa’s father and praises the elder Tokugawa’s leadership of the America-Japan Society. He asks that sympathy be conveyed to Iemasa’s mother and states that the embassy flag will be flown at half-mast.

subfiles.title: Letter conveying Hull’s condolences to Foreign Minister Arita
subfiles.about: Communicates the official American condolence message to Japan’s foreign minister.
subfiles.summary: Grew relays Hull’s sympathy on behalf of himself and the United States government. He adds that he wholeheartedly shares Hull’s feelings concerning the loss of Prince Tokugawa.

subfiles.title: Letter conveying Hull’s condolences to Prince Iemasa Tokugawa
subfiles.about: Asks Iemasa Tokugawa to communicate the official American condolence message to his family.
subfiles.summary: Grew quotes Hull’s tribute to the late prince as a humanitarian, statesman, and advocate of international friendship. He tells Iemasa that the same message is being sent to the foreign minister and adds his own sympathy.

subfiles.title: Hideomi Mori’s letter about the Tokugawa family’s appreciation
subfiles.about: Reports the Tokugawa family’s gratitude for the Grews’ sympathy and the embassy’s half-mast tribute.
subfiles.summary: Mori laments the loss of an important leader in international affairs. He reports that Iemasa Tokugawa and the family were deeply moved by the condolence letter and the unusual courtesy of flying the embassy flag at half-mast.

subfiles.title: America-Japan Society resolution on Prince Tokugawa
subfiles.about: Records the society’s tribute and sympathy after the death of its longtime president.
subfiles.summary: The resolution praises Tokugawa’s loyalty, character, international outlook, and sixteen years of leadership. It records the society’s affection, gratitude, and sorrow and presents its sympathy to his family. Joseph Clark Grew and Count Aisuke Kabayama sign in their capacities as honorary president and vice-president.

subfiles.title: Foreign Minister Arita’s acknowledgment of American condolences
subfiles.about: Thanks Hull and Grew for their expressions of sympathy and confirms delivery to the Tokugawa family.
subfiles.summary: Arita acknowledges Grew’s June 6 letter and expresses the Japanese government’s sincere thanks to Hull and Grew. He states that Hull’s message has been conveyed to Prince Tokugawa’s family.

subfiles.title: Japan Advertiser obituary: “Prince Tokugawa Taken by Death”
subfiles.about: Reports Prince Iesato Tokugawa’s death and reviews his public career, international work, family, and character.
subfiles.summary: The obituary says Tokugawa died at age seventy-six from heart trouble complicated by pneumonia and describes imperial honors, funeral plans, and prominent visitors. It recounts his succession to the Tokugawa house, education at Eton, leadership of the House of Peers, Red Cross work, overseas travel, and support for Japanese-American friendship. Statements by Yorinaga Matsudaira, Kunishige Tanaka, Joseph Grew, and Sir Robert Craigie emphasize his parliamentary record, English ability, international service, and commitment to peace.

subfiles.title: Japan Advertiser report: “Prince Tokugawa Buried with Rites”
subfiles.about: Describes Prince Tokugawa’s Buddhist funeral and burial at Kan'ei-ji.
subfiles.summary: The article follows the funeral procession from the Tokugawa residence in Sendagaya to Kan'ei-ji in Ueno and names relatives, military officers, imperial representatives, and other mourners. It reports that Tokugen Nagasawa officiated, about 3,000 people paid respects, and burial occurred in the family cemetery. The article also reproduces the America-Japan Society’s memorial resolution.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to pamphlet of a radio tribute to Prince Tokugawa
subfiles.about: Refers to a despatch enclosing copies of a July 5 radio tribute to Prince Tokugawa.
subfiles.summary: The sheet points to despatch No. 4901 in file 894.76/21. That despatch enclosed ten copies of a pamphlet containing the tribute broadcast to the United States.

subfiles.title: Department of State charge slip for file 894.48/73
subfiles.about: Records the charging or temporary removal of a document associated with file 894.48/73.
subfiles.summary: The page is a largely blank Department of State charge form. It identifies file number 894.48/73 but supplies no legible document description, recipient, or charge date.
